title: Market Surf Report

conditions.headline: Small bounce paddling out after two losing weeks; Brazil wipes out
conditions.summary: US futures are modestly higher as crude slips about 2 percent from near six-month highs, ahead of a huge week of Big Tech earnings and a Fed decision. Brazilian stocks are crashing after President Lula's surprise re-election.

sections.title: Futures & Overnight
items: S&P 500 futures are up about 0.3%, Nasdaq-100 futures about 0.3% and Dow futures about 0.5%, as of roughly 4:20 AM CT.
Friday the Dow fell more than 600 points and the S&P 500 slipped 0.5%, its second straight weekly loss.
WTI crude is down about 2% near $101 a barrel and Brent is near $110, as Qatari mediators head to Tehran.
The 10-year Treasury yield is near 4.99%; the dollar index is up about 0.1% near 101.8.
Gold is up about 0.4% near $4,020 an ounce; bitcoin is near $80,400, up about 0.3%.
VIX is near 19.6; Russell 2000 futures quotes were not available in our sources.
Asia was mixed: Hong Kong's Hang Seng rose, while Japan's Nikkei and South Korea's Kospi slipped.
Europe is roughly flat in early trade, with energy shares lagging as oil eases.

sections.title: Macro & Economic Calendar
items: No major US economic releases are scheduled today.
The Fed decides Wednesday at 1:00 PM CT; markets expect a hold at 3.75%–4.00% after September's hike, with a December hike still in play.
Bank of Canada, the ECB and the Bank of Japan also decide this week.
Middle East tension and oil remain the main macro driver, along with the November 3 midterm elections.

sections.title: Earnings
items: Verizon reports before the open today; consensus EPS is about $1.27.
After the close: Cadence Design Systems, Celestica and Welltower.
Celestica consensus is about $2.99 EPS on $5.48 billion in revenue.
Roughly a third of S&P 500 companies report this week, led by Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon.

sections.title: Stocks in the News
items: XP (XP Inc.): -46% — Brazilian brokers and banks plunge after President Lula's surprise re-election.
ITUB (Itaú Unibanco): -28% — Brazil's biggest bank leads the selloff in US-listed Brazilian shares.
PBR (Petrobras): -24% — investors fear more state influence over the oil giant under Lula.
NU (Nu Holdings): -22% — the Brazilian digital bank slides with the rest of Brazil.
SGRY (Surgery Partners): +21% — reports say Bon Secours Mercy Health is in late-stage talks to buy a majority stake.
TSLA (Tesla): +2% — Barclays upgraded it to Overweight with a $450 target.
CRWV (CoreWeave) and NBIS (Nebius): -3% — neocloud worries after Musk predicted consolidation; both are down more than 30% this month.
MRNA (Moderna): about -9% to -11% — selling continues after Phase 3 melanoma vaccine data and a downgrade to Sell at Rothschild & Co Redburn.

sections.title: Business News
items: Brazil: Lula won a fourth term, defying polls; the iShares Brazil ETF is indicated down more than 20% pre-market.
SpaceX: Musk says the company closed $40 billion in debt financing to buy GPUs, though Bloomberg says pricing talks continued late Sunday.
Instacart: Uber walked away from acquisition talks, and DoorDash has held preliminary talks, according to reports.
Audi plans a roughly $4 billion factory in Georgia; SoftBank picked Malaysia for $50 billion of technology investments.
S&P Dow Jones Indices will overhaul how it scores growth and value stocks before December 21, affecting at least $375 billion in tracking funds.

sections.title: What to Watch Today
items: 8:30 AM CT open: whether the bounce holds after two losing weeks for the S&P 500.
Brazil contagion: Brazilian ADRs and the iShares Brazil ETF, plus any spillover to emerging markets.
Crude near $100: oil is the swing factor for yields, which sit just under 5% on the 10-year.

sections.title: Earnings This Week
items: Mon: Verizon (VZ), before open — wireless subscriber growth.
Mon: Cadence Design Systems (CDNS), after close — chip-design demand tied to AI.
Tue: UPS (UPS) and Boeing (BA), before open — package volumes; Boeing's jet deliveries and cash burn.
Tue: Visa (V), after close — consumer spending trends.
Wed: GE Vernova (GEV), before open — power-equipment orders for data centers.
Wed: Alphabet (GOOGL), after close — Google Cloud growth after 82% last quarter.
Wed: Microsoft (MSFT), after close — Azure growth against roughly 45% guidance.
Thu: Eli Lilly (LLY), Merck (MRK) and Caterpillar (CAT), before open — weight-loss drug sales, pharma pipeline, machinery demand.
Thu: Amazon (AMZN), after close — sales versus its $197–$202 billion forecast and AWS growth.
Thu: Intel (INTC), after close — margins and foundry progress; consensus EPS about $0.28.
Fri: ExxonMobil (XOM), Chevron (CVX) and AbbVie (ABBV), before open — energy profits with oil near $100.

sections.title: Economic Calendar This Week
items: Mon: No major US releases.
Tue 9:00 AM CT: Conference Board consumer confidence (Oct) — consensus 80.0, prior 81.9.
Wed 8:45 AM CT: Bank of Canada decision — a hike to 2.50% is expected.
Wed 1:00 PM CT: Fed decision, press conference 1:30 PM CT — hold at 3.75%–4.00% expected.
Thu 7:30 AM CT: Q3 GDP first estimate — consensus about 3.1% annualized; September PCE inflation — core +0.2% m/m expected.
Thu: ECB decision (hold expected) and, Thursday evening CT, the Bank of Japan.
Fri: Fed speakers Mary Daly and Alberto Musalem.
Note: the busiest week of earnings season, with month-end on Friday and the November 3 midterms next week.

sources.title: Reuters via Investing.com: futures edge up as oil falls
Benzinga: futures rise, stocks in focus
StockTitan: earnings calendar week of Oct 26
European shares flat as investors eye earnings

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Monday, October twenty-sixth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Market Surf Report. Riding shotgun on the cabana deck is my co-anchor, Gus the wonder dog, freshly towel-dried from his sunrise swim. Give the lineup a Monday howdy, Gus! Let's check the swell. After two losing weeks, a small set is rolling in on the Dawn Patrol. S and P five hundred futures are up about three tenths of a percent. Nasdaq futures are up about the same, and Dow futures about half a percent. Crude oil is down about two percent, near one hundred and one dollars a barrel. The ten year Treasury yield sits near four point nine nine percent. Gold is just above four thousand dollars, and bitcoin is near eighty thousand. The VIX is near nineteen and a half. Asia was mixed, and Europe is flat. Wind and weather: no major US data today. On the tide chart, Verizon reports before the bell. After the close we get Cadence Design Systems, Celestica and Welltower. Now the lineup, and Brazil is having a gnarly wipeout. President Lula won a surprise re-election, and US-listed Brazilian shares are crashing. X P is down about forty-six percent. Itau Unibanco is down about twenty-eight percent, and Petrobras is down about twenty-four percent. On the bright side, Surgery Partners is up about twenty-one percent on reports a hospital group is in late-stage talks to buy a majority stake. Cowabunga, that's a real wave! That calls for a treat, Gus! Here you go, buddy! Tesla is up about two percent after a Barclays upgrade. And Moderna is down about nine to eleven percent after its melanoma vaccine data fell short of high hopes, plus a downgrade. Beach talk. Elon Musk says SpaceX closed forty billion dollars of debt to buy A I chips, though Bloomberg says pricing talks were still going late Sunday. And Uber walked away from talks to buy Instacart. Sets to watch: whether the bounce holds after the eight thirty A M Central open, any Brazil spillover, and oil near one hundred dollars. Time for the week's swell forecast. Tuesday brings Boeing and U P S in the morning, Visa after the close, and consumer confidence at nine A M Central. Wednesday the Fed decides at one P M Central, with a hold expected, and Alphabet and Microsoft report after the close. Thursday at seven thirty A M Central we get third quarter G D P and P C E inflation. Eli Lilly and Caterpillar report that morning, and Amazon and Intel after the close. Friday, Exxon Mobil and Chevron wrap it up. The biggest waves: the Fed and Microsoft and Alphabet, all on Wednesday. Want a read on any stock, E T F or futures contract? Type it into the Check a Wave box on the page, and Surf Daddy will call it for you. This is information, not advice. This is Surf Daddy and Gus the wonder dog saying, if in doubt, paddle out!
